author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can narrow the veterinarian list to one specialty by address
summary: Both veterinarian list forms, the paged page and the machine-readable list, accept an optional specialty in the address and list only the veterinarians holding it. Matching is whole-name and ignores case; a blank value is ignored, and paging keeps the narrowing.
acceptance_criteria: Given a specialty name, when /vets.html?specialty=<name> is requested, then the page lists only veterinarians holding that specialty, and paging applies to the narrowed list.
Given a specialty name, when /vets?specialty=<name> is requested, then the machine-readable list contains only veterinarians holding that specialty.
Given a specialty name differing from a held specialty only by letter case, when either form is narrowed to it, then it matches.
Given only the beginning of a specialty name, when either form is narrowed to it, then no veterinarian matches (whole-name match, not prefix).
Given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either form is narrowed to it, then the usual page or document is returned with HTTP 200 and an empty veterinarian list.
Given an empty or whitespace-only specialty value, when either form is requested, then the result equals the request without the parameter.

Given no specialty parameter, when either form is requested, then it behaves as today: the page lists every veterinarian a page at a time, the machine-readable list returns every veterinarian unpaged.
Given more veterinarians holding the specialty than fit on one page, when a narrowed page is rendered, then every pagination link carries the specialty so later pages stay narrowed.
A veterinarian holding several specialties is listed when any one of them matches (PRD edge case 2).
A veterinarian holding no specialty never appears in a narrowed list (PRD edge case 3).
Neither form gains a form, dropdown, or other page control for the specialty (PRD edge case 4).
non_goals: Free-text veterinarian search, and pet or visit search (NG-9 as narrowed)
Any form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing a specialty; a visible control may come as a follow-up request
Narrowing by more than one specialty at once, or by any attribute other than specialty
notes: Owner absent; narrowest readings taken per the intake. IDs: REQ-VET-003 is the filter; REQ-VET-004 is the fresh requirement reinstating the /vets machine-readable list (intake decision 2); REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn, Superseded entry updated. REQ-VET-004's contract is today's behavior; the no-parameter criterion and theVetJsonListShouldReturnEveryVetWhenNoSpecialtyIsGiven pin it. NG-9 narrowed per intake decision 1, recorded in docs/adr/2026-11-04-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md; docs/adr/README.md index row is outside this agent's write scope and needs adding by its owner. Open questions recorded in docs/prd.md, not in the contract: (a) whether padding around a non-blank specialty name is trimmed; implementer must not decide it silently; (b) whether a narrowed page labels the active specialty; this slice adds no label. Unchanged existing behavior: a page number past the narrowed range behaves as an out-of-range page does today.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the vet feature package and the owner-search pattern (paged Spring Data derived query on the feature's repository, controller binds and delegates; OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith, grep-resolved, IDE oracle not connected). New ground recorded in docs/system-design.md: Contracts rows for VetController, VetRepository, Vet, Specialty, Vets, CacheConfiguration now carry REQ-VET-003/REQ-VET-004; an Invariants paragraph 'Specialty narrowing'; a new § Scale and Load table (unfiltered and narrowed vet list rows); a Security Context input line and a Threat Model row for caller-chosen specialty text; the obsolete Known Defect 'machine-readable route serves no requirement' removed since REQ-VET-004 reinstates the route. ADR docs/adr/2026-11-04-specialty-filter-as-uncached-repository-query.md records the decision: matching is a derived query on VetRepository with case ignored in the generated SQL (vendor-independent, unlike the PostgreSQL owner-search defect), one paged variant for /vets.html and one unpaged variant for /vets, and NO @Cacheable on the narrowed methods so caller text never keys the unbounded 'vets' cache. Unfiltered paths stay exactly as today (cached findAll() / findAll(Pageable)). Suggested shape (implementer may refine names): findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) and findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String); Distinct keeps a vet listed once even if it held two specialties differing only by case. Controller: optional String specialty request param on both handlers; null/blank -> unfiltered branch (binding normalization per architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog Web controller row); any other value passed through untrimmed (narrowest reading of PRD open question on padding). Model gains the normalized specialty (null when absent) for the template. Template: every pagination link built with Thymeleaf link-expression parameters, e.g. @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encodes the value and omits it when null; no control or label is added (PRD edge case 4).
integration_points: Binding, GET /vets.html: request-scoped scalars only — int page (existing) and optional String specialty; no persisted type is bound.
Binding, GET /vets: optional String specialty request-scoped scalar; response stays the Vets wrapper with existing content negotiation.

Double, repository boundary: none — the PRD-named behavior tests drive the real VetRepository against the seeded H2 database through MockMvc in a new VetControllerIntegrationTests (@SpringBootTest + @AutoConfigureMockMvc, precedent CrashControllerIntegrationTests / ClinicServiceTests). Matching semantics live in the query, so a stubbed repository cannot test them. Seed data covers single match (radiology: Leary, Stevens), several specialties (Douglas), and no-specialty vets (Carter, Jenkins).

Double, paging test: insert extra radiology vets with JdbcTemplate inside a @Transactional test (rolled back) so more than one page exists; request only narrowed pages there, because unfiltered reads are cached and would retain rolled-back rows.
Double, framework transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned harness (testing-principles § Mocking Policy). Existing VetControllerTests and its @MockitoBean stubs stay untouched; add no new Mockito stubs.

findings.description: The conditional `${specialty != null} ? @{/vets.html(page=X,specialty=${specialty})} : @{/vets.html(page=X)}` is repeated verbatim across five pagination links (numbered, first, previous, next, last), differing only in the page expression. The Control Flow checklist treats a conditional repeated across sibling template elements as duplication. Each href is now over 120 columns, so the page expression is hard to spot in each copy and a future change to the narrowing rule must be made five times. Swept the class: the only other repeated conditional in the change set is these five hrefs; the controller's two `presentOrNull` call sites are not duplicated logic.
findings.fix: Compute the href once per link through a small Thymeleaf fragment that takes the page number, for example `th:fragment="pageHref(target)"` holding the single conditional, and reference it from the five links. Keep the link-expression parameter form that system-design.md § Contracts requires, with no preprocessing.

Secrets: `grep -i -E '^\+.*(password|secret|token|apikey|api_key|credential)'` over the changeset hits only a system-design.md prose line describing the existing environment-supplied datasource credentials; no credential is added.

Supply chain: no build file in the change set (`changeset.py --name-only | grep -F build.gradle` returns nothing), so no dependency moves. No dependency vulnerability scan runs, a standing gap listed in docs/security-principles.md § Standing Gaps; the resolved runtime set from `./gradlew dependencies` shows Spring Boot 4.1.2, Jackson (tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind) 3.1.7, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, Hibernate 7.4.13.Final. The current page number, and the first/previous/next/last controls at the boundaries, would then render as a link beside their th:unless plain-text or disabled-icon sibling. The suite does not assert that the current page is not a link (grep -n -i -E 'first|previous|currentPage' on VetControllerIntegrationTests.java shows only the narrowed-first-page href pattern), so green tests do not clear it.
